review:
As always, the newest version of FM is bit better than the earlier one. I have played since 93 I think and still enjoy the game. However, I don't purchase every new FM, only every second. Last one I played was fm19 and fm17 before that. It seems the developers are bit lazy for bringing in new features and removing or fixing features that don't quite work and therefore getting every second new version is enough. 

An example: The team talk is still practically the same as it was 4 years ago. New comments are rare and you get very quickly bored when asked the same questions over and over and over again. AI is poor in the questions as well. Last question before my CL final was a random team in the same league putting a random player on transfer list and asking if I agree with the decision or not. The impact of answers seems minor as well yet it features now more often than ever. At least in the new version you can safely let the assistant manager handle them not risking everybody getting angry when they say silly things. 

Another (small) example: Negotiating a new contract with your club. As it has been years now, they don't budge at all. They offer something regardless of how well you have managed the team and asking even "one tick" more results them just offering the original sum until you either accept it or don't get new contract. So you can make the team best in the world winning CL many times in a row and the salary stays at the same, or you leave. Just a minor thing but annoying.

So basically a very good game as always with minor improvements from FM19 (match engine is really cool from time to time and removing % and putting hearts in condition for example is way better and realistic) but if SI wants us to buy every new version coming up yearly, they should have little more effort than just updating the database

I finally upgraded to FM21 after skipping FM19 & 20 - mostly it was the xG feature that piqued my interest, but I also like to update every so often for little things like competition rule/qualification changes, refreshing rosters, etc. Coming from FM18, I've been pleasantly surprised at some of the new features added in FM21 - not only do I really enjoy the xG thing, I love the overall improvement in what I'd call "realism": The interaction with staff continues to get better and better, the way staff and management present you with reports and call meetings is awesome, and the scouting meetings before transfer windows are so damn cool. It all combines to make you feel like you're actually a manager and not just playing a game. I'm at around 230 hours of FM21 and I'm still constantly finding myself engaging with new things. 

Last, I'd just like to share my experience/thoughts on scum-saving. For the most part during my thousands of hours of FM over the years, I felt like I was pretty fair about reloading matches - I only tended to do it if I had a bad injury to a star I'd just signed, or conceded a BS glitch/bug goal, etc. Sometimes if I was having a bad day and fired up FM only to be down 4-0 to Man City in the 35th minute I'd just Ctl-Alt-Delete and replay the match a few days later. But with my new save in FM21, I've been experimenting with a strict no-save-scumming policy, and it's added a whole new compelling element to my gameplay. I had a real stinker of a game against Newcastle (5-0 I think) - the sort of game I'd have been tempted to reload in the past - and a day later my players refunded the supporters' tickets for the match. How cool is that!? I also got to within one bad result of getting sacked, and had to get something away at Sheffield Utd - what a nerve-racking match that was! My boys pulled out a 3-1 win to keep me alive, and we had a short run of good form to finish the season, allowing me to get the transfer reinforcements I desperately needed. 

So TL;DR: FM is hands down the best sports management sim on the market, I felt it was well worth the money to upgrade from FM18 to FM21, and if you've never experimented with a no-save-scum policy - give it a whirl. I think you'll find it rewarding.

The best football manager yet.

Oh and still no improvements to online play, FM would take off to another market if it brought back FM Live, such a good game that was way ahead of its time but the stubborn Miles poo-poo's it everytime it is brought up.

I love the game, except for one major flaw; the match engine's hard coded bad streak / good streak mechanic. No matter what you do after a good run there will be one match a season, veterans will know the match I am talking about, where all of your players become limp fish on the pitch and lose form at exactly the same time. And before the hardcore fans come out and say "oh it's complacency" no, it's not there is not a single player with a complacent body language and everything has been done to reduce potential complacency. Messi's dribbling turns into Peter Crouch, Kompany's defending becomes like Ozil, and world class players just watch the ball go past them, hit the woodwork all of the time, miss every 1o1, cross the ball into defenders more often, pass the ball long straight back to the other team even though you have defensive short passing on, injuries to the best players etc etc. It's pretty much the same as the FIFA scripted mechanic. 

Then after this one match, the next 10 or so will become extremely difficult, and no change in tactic, roles, swapping in players, match talks, press talks... nothing will change this mechanic. The form is hard coded in the game and there's nothing you can do about it. Some people will say this is like real life; teams go through bad forms, and that is true, but the question is do we want to play a game which forces a bad form onto you which is completely out of your control, or would you prefer to have some influence over the bad form? This bad form will hit once a season on average, no matter what you do, consistent rotation or no rotation, changing tactics to adapt to the AI, or keeping them consistent it doesn't matter. Alot of people also respond to this criticism by saying, "the AI adapts to your tactics after a while if you are winning", and the AI does change their tactics, but them changing their tactics has nothing to do with why your team suddenly can't pass forwards without an interception, or they stand and watch the ball go past, or dribble straight into the opposition players, or hit the woodwork or get injured at 300% rate than normal, or suddenly can't make a first touch anymore, or their crosses hit the opposition and create a corner and you know all 1o1's will end badly during this form. Most of this has nothing to do with the opposition tactics, just because they went counter attack, shouldn't mean my players all lose 10 to their dribbling, passing, first touch, positioning stat for 10 games. 

The next response to this I see often is "what incentive would SI have to put such a mechanic in the game?"
Because commercial incentives developers have in keeping their customers coming back every year. SI can't make the same game every year with an updated roster and a couple differences in the UI and match engine without generating an addiction in their customers. This bad/good form streak creates an actual dopamine psychological addiction, similar to loot boxes in other games or player cards in FIFA. The reward in this game is good form, and a feeling that you have overcome something which was prior out of your control. When you regain the good form streak, where now all your players dribble like Messi, and shoot like Lewandoswki, you feel like you are responsible. 

The human condition of contrast effect (is the enhancement or diminishment, relative to normal, of perception, cognition or related performance as a result of successive (immediately previous) or simultaneous exposure to a stimulus of lesser or greater value in the same dimension) creates a much larger sense of achievement when we get into a good form relative to the out of control bad form. Doubly it has an additional contrast effect as we feel like the game is out of our control during the bad form (external locus of control), and in control (internal locus of control) during the good form creating a massively exaggerated sense of being in control during the good form and we experience a dopamine feedback loop for the good form as we, without cognitive awareness, compare it to the experience and external locus of control of the bad form. 

SI used to have an addiction rating in the game based on the number of hours you played, they are well aware of how dopamine responds to this contrast effect of psychological states of external and internal locus of control. I worked in insurance gamification, so even more morally bankrupt than EA with FIFA, and they are very aware of mechanics for creating addictions in the customers. It's a business, it would be poor business management and product development if they didn't find a way to get customers coming back every year. SI would without a doubt have KPI's and OKR's and targets for customer retention every year, so the department responsible for hitting these targets would be probably the ones responsible for keeping these frustrating game mechanics in the game. Add to this that this bad form also creates an artificial difficulty spike which keeps the game engaging for veterans, who would stop buying the game if they found it too easy every iteration. 

This mechanic is actually not as bad as in FM2020, but it is still there and I doubt they will be removing it any time soon. I probably wouldn't have played this one for so long without the sense of achievement I had in being better at this one than FM20 which had even more bad form/good form mechanics. But my skeptical mind tells me they make each iteration in a rotation of difficulty to keep that addiction fed. FM22 will probably be more difficult again, and FM23 will be easier, so they generate a long term meta contrast effect, and we feel more in control in this version relative to the last so we enjoy it again, then it's too easy so they make the next game more difficult and frustrating again. Cycle repeats. It's actually good game design if you don't notice it, but once you notice it, you can't really go back in good faith realizing you are just actually psychologically addicted to the cleverly crafted dopamine cycles. 

And if you think it's not possible to be psychologically addicted to a game, gamblers on the slot machines have been shown to have actual similar dopamine responses to winning as people have to hard drugs. Think about that before you buy a game that intentionally gets you addicted. SI are no better than gambling companies, they just use a different psychological effect to get you addicted, just instead of money as the reward they give you a sense of inflated control relative to the bad streak.. which come to think of it is the same as a slot machine. To your brain there is no difference between winning money and winning a sense of control, they represent the same thing. 

The problem is if they made this mechanic transparent, it wouldn't have the same addictive effect, the same way knowing that a slot machine will ALWAYS hard coded give you a return of 96% on your $1, most people who realized this don't gamble. This game does the same with their hard coding of streaks, and once it's become transparent it doesn't have appeal anymore. So they need to keep it intransparent to keep the game engaging, and we will forever be frustrated at that bad streak until we liberate ourselves with the knowledge that this bad streak is intentionally there to keep you interested, and spending more money.

It pains me to write this but after spending more than 400 hours I have to admit: it's a poorly designed game with artifical difficulty spikes designed to keep players engaged. You can be the by far best team in the league and you will always have a seasonal rival (undocumented in-game) which will keep the pace with you. You can be a heavy-weight in a small league and there will be a team which is not better than any other in competitions which will go with the same results as you. 

Worst part when the game decides that it should boost your real rival. I have just one example of it: playing in UPL with Shakhtar I managed to finish the season with 28 wins and 2 draws in the 30 games. Guess what was the gap with Dynamo Kiev? 2 points. The third place was like 20 points lower. A season before I lost the league to Vorskla - it had lost points in 4 games through the whole season and my only loss was to them. I had numerous finishings in previous seasons with different teams when on the last match day the leader was losing, my team coming second won and then the third team became the first on goal difference, winning 5-0 and scoring its last goal on the last minutes in injury time. I get that it happens in football, see Man City and Aguero, but not in the course of couple of seasons in a row.

Apart of that the game is addicting as ever although SI doesn't care for bug fixing (top managers have like perpetual contracts, in my 15 season save Simeone, Conte, OGS, Pochettino and Flick ALL were managing their starting cubs) and their UI designer clearly hates people - I can't find any reason to make the UI overloaded mess in dark purple color. In 2021 SI didn't even care to add additional skins leaving it to fans. Really, you become so lazy? You had to tweak a couple of lines of code to do that.

Match engine looks much better until you realize that it relies heavily on the patterns. If you get that patterns, you can exploit it, and if you want to keep it natural you will face artificial difficulty spikes. Maybe in 2000s it was the same, I don't know, it all felt like an unscripted free flow and now you can guess the outcome of episode 90% times the 3D field appears.

Tactics make no sense, as you can't play defensive football relying to soak the pressure - it's instantly punished by the opposition. Players with 5 in long shots suddenly pull of Roberto Carlos if you play defensive and there is no way to explain it but the match engine flaws. If the game decides that it's time to score, it will score. To play attacking you should do counter-intuitive things (deep defensive line and low pressure against the last team in a league is a must or you will be heavily beaten with the magic 30-meter screamers).

On top of that you have the SI community forums with extremely gatekeeping audience which is intolerable to any criticism of their game. Moderators delete negative comments claiming they welcome meaningful discussion and constructive criticism. Like, I'm a paying customer who gets banned for stating that I'm not that happy with what I've payed for. In all my years online I've never seen more toxic and hostile community - even Reddit is friendly and supportive in comparison. Think twice before sponsoring it. I was a big fan of FM in 2005 - 2012 editions, I haven't really played for 8 years and I had over 700 extremely frustrating and unrewarding hours in 2020/21 versions. I won't buy it before they fix the UI and fire their UI designer. I can't possibly recommend the game which is made with the goal to frustrate the players and encourage exploits.

I'm not a soccer fan. I don't watch soccer, never played it, I don't even like sports. 
As a strategy game fan, this is enjoyable on almost every level. You have thousands upon thousands of decisions to make, you can change your team however you want, and it's basically just making your own story.
Football manager allows you to play the game no matter what your skill level is at strategy games, with options to make the game more or less involved by having other people take an aspect of the game and do it for you.
If you really enjoy learning things and studying information, absolutely get this game, even if you don't have an interest in football. Those who love strategy games and simulators will really enjoy this.

The only notable improvement to the game is in the match engine, especially the trophy presentations and added match day detail. However, there are still annoying bugs that irritate me, the main ones being:
-Wingers running at goal from out wide, electing to shoot from the tightest of angles rather than pass.
-Attacking players ballooning headers miles over the bar from point blank range for no apparent reason.
-Players inexplicably running at half pace and losing out on a ball which even your 90 year old nan could get to.

The changes in how player fatigue is shown seems unnecessary, as the hearts have replaced the more detailed and faultless percentage system. 

Now for what has really annoyed me: player attributes/ development:
 
- I have bought various highly rated youngsters for my Liverpool team and NONE of them have improved whilst at my club. In fact they have all declined substantially, despite me giving them adequate match experience, having near perfect training facilities/ coaches and also strong mentoring groups. However, young players at other clubs seem to improve dramatically, despite their training facilities and coaches being of a poorer standard and the players competing at a lower level. 

- Another issue is the fact that players ability to dribble always decreases by around 3-4 points as soon as they hit age 27 for some weird reason. Is this a bug or based on real life?

- The little green arrows next to a players attributes never seem to noticeably correspond to an increase in stats, however, if a red arrow appears, the attribute will usually decrease! Is this a bug?

- Individual training has no effect on a players attributes! For example a player will often train on defensive positioning yet their positioning rating will then decrease! 

Please get back to me on these issues, as its ruining the game for me.

Finally, the same bug that has annoyed me in the last 5 iterations of football manager: Player transfers. PSG, Barca, Real Madrid, Man City and Chelsea seem to throw hundreds of millions of pound around like confetti, UNLESS its for one of your players, in which case they will low ball you with an offer which is half the players market value! Attempting to buy a player means you will be quoted 120 million for a 20 year old with zero match experience, yet no one will bid more than 30 million for your world class centre mid. I thought SI might have rectified this issue by now, but sadly not!

Hours played should speak for itself.

I am doing a pentagon challenge (all 5 champions leagues) to thoroughly test this game. I will edit at the end. So for a very short version, this review is negative, but not as a complete let-down - to me this is a 5/10 game. The philosophy is steering back into the right direction, it can be fun once again and there are certain improvements. But there's so many small things wrong, considering we pay full price for basically a database update and some minor UI improvements every year, there is no excuse.  Also additions to the game are starting to feel like bloat, rather than extras.

Anyway, for the long part - I'm a huge football manager/championship manager fan, I'm one of those old fans who made the game what it is, sinking thousands of hours into it and recommending it left and right. From Bojinov to Yaya Sanogo, I've been along for the ride. At some point the games lost their "fun" for me in exchange for realism and I stopped buying them. 

Starting with the positive, I should say this is the first FM I've actually had fun with since 14. I don't regret 15 and 16 but they were more of a challenge I got through than a game I had fun with. I also tried 20 and hated it. The match engine to me is a huge improvement over 20 and even a huge improvement over old ones where you had to play around certain huge weaknesses, such as very poor striker movement. In this one it feels like you have a choice. Long passes are back and are no longer just a tool for direct, counter-attacking football. Fullbacks actually contribute to the match and aren't a burden. Your tactics, players and decisions are more in control than the code of the game. 

The graphics improvements are also nice. These two things alone show a shift in what should have been the philosophy from the start, focus on graphics and keep the fun. 

HOWEVER, the game is riddled with small bullshit that just kills all the enjoyment when you encounter it. The biggest one for me is that it can get way too easy - set a strategy, get the right players for it, have a bit of depth and watch the game play itself. There's no challenge in getting the right players - if in previous FMs it was ridiculously hard to buy or sell specific players (such as in smaller leagues) in this one its hilariously easy. You can easily form a team to challenge the champion's league with the budget of a second tier italian side (albeit not with that reputation, since players seem almost 100% motivated by reputation on whether they move). Playing in a lower league? Get a 100k $ transfer budget or free up some wage budget and you will easily buy out the entire league. I like the "ask agent for availability" thing, I really do, but since transfers seem so much easier, it just adds even more ease. Spam it on players and you can essentially have an overview of the exact price of every player on the market. 

The second most annoying thing for me has to be the end of every match. Now I felt I was getting scored on/scoring way too much towards the end and I looked at the stats - in a single season I had 60 goals total scored and scored against me. Out of those 60 a staggering 22 were in the last 10 minutes. More than a third!!! An even more staggering 8 of those were AFTER 90 minutes! Nearly 10%. My players were determined, ok with stamina, nothing special and I made no big changes to tactics at the end. I monitored the AI and it rarely did anything either. The second season I played the case was roughly the same. 

Injuries - I feel like the frequency of injuries is ok and players recover realistically. But for some reason small injuries, i.e. a 2-3 day tight groin, a cold or a virus are ridiculously common. This is quite annoying. 

It also feeds into my next point, which is the vast amount of bloat and micromanagement. I've never liked press conferences, but I give them a try every time since I feel its unrealistic to just ignore the press. But these gestures just add more bloat to what felt already like bloat. Same with player interactions - I try, I really do, but by the 6th time your entire team is unhappy you won't sell your only good striker for pennies with no possible replacement and you just have to go through the entire conversation over and over with no real choice, just pressing the same buttons, adding gestures is again, bloat on top of bloat. The UI has been discussed enough, but its the same case for me. I feel these things take away from the core game and create a lot more opportunity for small problems that break the enjoyment.

Some more, minor issues - wingbacks are hilariously overpowered in the right setting, easily scoring a hattrick with long shots outside the box. For that matter, crazy long shots are still here and still way too common, getting a "oooh! magnificent goal!!" from an unlikely player twice a game really ruins the fun of scoring them. Trust me, get a wingback with okish technique and set him to stay wide and shoot - watch as he gets unmarked, never pressured and smashes ridiculous shots over and over. Lastly, when a team finds space it will do so over and over again and trying to close that space by adjusting tactics will rarely work. On the other hand, if you find a weakness in the AI it will basically never cover it - hence if you score 2 in the first half you'll probably score 5-6 by the end. This especially ruins one of the most fun parts of FM, developing youngsters, as a youngster underperforming can easily make you concede a ton of goals on its own. 

Now I could overlook all of this, I really could, but we're getting sold essentially the same game every year. And millions are supporting it. How many developers can boast a 100% guaranteed revenue stream? So with that in mind, to have these small mistakes and oversights is just not acceptable. So many of the reviews to me seem like "well it's football manager and its functional, so five stars", which misses the point. I think reviews should serve to point the game in the right direction and to me that's thorough testing rather than changing the already great UI or adding more options for interactions.

FM21 is not a bad game. But, if you have 20, don't waste your money on 21.

Much like VAR irl, realism and accuracy have been shoehorned in over an enjoyable experience:
1) Love hearts and thumbs up for fitness and condition. Why?! Yes, I know real managers don't have exact numbers but it looked so much better and was so much simpler to have %.

2) My biggest gripe. The match day screen. I have no idea what developers were thinking here. There's been a great UX for years imo and I get the need for renovation but the most important information I need; my players performance, their condition, and body language have now been squashed to the bottom of the screen and replaced with inane stats.

3) Team talks. Did the screen really have to change from a list to a 'room'? It's added nothing to the experience and isn't instantly clear if what I've said is motivating or not.

4) Body language. Just a gimmick. I used it once or twice and now ignore it.

If you're a sporadic buyer of FMs then this is a good choice to come back in to. I'm sure loads of people will enjoy the game and it is still fun. It's just not as good as 20, and nowhere near the classics (07, 11, 12, etc)

Football Manager 2021 hasn’t really rocked the boat in terms of enhancing the matchday gaming experience from last year. Games are as  difficult as ever to manage, and the minutiae of detail is just as overwhelming as always. Rather than a complete overhaul, there are numerous minor tweaks in Football Manager 2021, affecting tactical exploration and simulation. This time around, energy levels in particular seem to play a greater role, presumably to combat previously effective pressing tactics. In other words,  you can’t rely on your tried-and-tested methods from last year to get by.

Football Manager 2021‘s biggest change seems to come in the way that you, as a Manager, communicate. Gone are the meaningless emotions while addressing people; instead, your decisions are broken down into what really matters. While talking to players, the boardroom or press, you can respond in a much more clear way. You’ll be able to choose from responses that are positive, negative, convincing, or even backing down. Better yet, the intended meaning of everything you say is clearly laid out.

The communication overhaul really adds a lot to how you are judged as a manager in Football Manager 2021. Yes, results are still important, but you can really change the parameters of what your personal success is. If you aren’t doing especially well but are achieving the promises you have set out, you will be given more time.

This happened to me; in my first season of managing, I had slightly underachieved. But because I had delivered on my promise to repair the financial damage of the over bloated squad, I wasn’t kicked out at the end of the season where I might’ve been in previous instalments. The next season, having been able to gain control of the finances, I was able to cultivate success. This is a new experience for me in a Football Manager game; a series I’ve been playing for over a decade. While I may have improved the finances of a club before, I have never overtly communicated my goals to the boardroom and insisted on time to deliver.

Football Manager 2021 has done something that great managers do: it has acknowledged its weaknesses and improved upon them without completely rocking the boat. It still feels truly familiar as a Football Manager game, but the overhaul to expectations and communication makes for a more coherent and impactful experience. There’s more of a focus on what you say and do in your role as a manager and, over seasons, your performance is better judged. It makes a real difference to how the game can play out. The matchday experience may not be massively improved, but the improved focus elsewhere makes a real difference. For anyone who truly likes to get into the role of manager, Football Manager 2021 is a must.

I'm a long time fan of SI's Football Manager games. They are by far the best in the market for football managing sims. Unfortunately, years have caught up to the software and it evolved into something else.

First, huge props to programmers having to deal with 20 years of legacy code, dubious frameworks and all other challenges of preserving and upgrading this enormous project. Development cycle of these games isn't long enough for meaningful changes and bug fixing. It's very hard to come up with something new, implementing it and having it completely tested on a yearly basis which could lead into things getting very stale and unexpected exploits appearing. There are also problems bleeding from one yearly version to next and so on.

These games suffer mostly from years and years of problem solving and innovating for the sake of innovation and bigger sales. Because of many overpowered exploits, or sometimes need to bring something new each year, things get overly complicated and some features get gutted. For example, in older versions corners were overpowered, so to make them more realistic we now have set piece routines that need to be set up before every single match if you want to have a chance at scoring them. Of course, you can save those routines but they are dependent on your players that you rotate almost every single match every season. Training was very simple and somewhat effective, but to add some sauce it got reworked and now it's kinda impossible to mold players to your will, improving specific attributes needed to take them to a new level. Meanwhile AI has almost free reign in developing their wonderkids. "Realism" is used at will to justify many creative decisions. Yet FM presents unrealistic scenarios all the time. Not only in match engine, but for example with man management. Would a player with loyal personality throw a fit after bid from a barely higher reputable team gets rejected? Would professional personalities try to turn whole dressing room against manager for not getting a contract they required with astronomical demands? To me at least, fun is much more important than the realism.

The challenge of FM games can be as difficult as you wish. Everything is possible with enough time and dedication. There are pre-made tactics which are so overpowered you don't even need to build any, if that's how you wish to manage. As time passes the games sadly boil down to recruitment (having better players than the rest) and going through the same motions which is inherently the biggest flaw of designing games like these. Unfortunately they will eventually become a chore regardless of how fun the challenge started. 

My frustration mostly comes from encountering same irritating things that kill the fun for me:
[list]
    [*]Transfers are a nightmare. If you are already very rich club you have nothing to worry about. But if you care about managing finances, you will have to deal with disgusting demands of players and AI teams. AI teams will lowball you when buying and rip you off completely when selling. AI teams will trade fairly between themselves and players will accept much lower contracts compared to what they demand from you. Worst part is that other teams will destroy your squad harmony and upset your biggest performers in order to buy them, only to not play them more than 10 games over 3 years before selling them on a bloated contract.
    [*]Wingers waiting for defenders to cover them, so they can blast a cross right into those defenders leading to corner number 53.
    [*]The amount of micromanaging stuff. You do have option of delegating things to other staff members but they will always do a below par job. Letting your assistant manager lead training could sometimes damage your match preparations and lead to multiple season long injuries. This is a management game, yes, but the amount of control and systems is simply very high and to play optimally you simply have to utilise them all
    [*]In former games, you could simply stack as much Brazilian and Argentinian wonderkids as you want. To nerf this, their wonderkinds became much more expensive and luxurious. So to bypass this, you simply resort to buying cheap Colombian, Peruvian, Chilean (all other South American really) and Eastern European wonderkids.
    [*]Promises to players when buying them are really stupid. Sometimes they will require to play in a role you randomly set on your tactic last match when experimenting. You might never even play that role again and that player probably didn't even play that role ever before. Yet if you don't fulfill those promises, whole squad will turn against you.
    [*]Squad dynamics, morale and player personality systems being completely out of whack. Get out of CL groups as an Eastern European team for 4 years in a row? Say that your goals is getting out of groups again in team meeting and they will jump their guns, get abysmal morale and whatnot thinking it's unrealistic. Every player no matter the personality is just a mercenary that will turn heel at first chance. There's rarely one club players among talented wonderkids (possible if you are 5 star reputation team), and the only thing personality can tell you is how likely will those players improve in the future (if they have potential).
    [*]Reputation system is a bad. You could be winning CL every season for 10 years and your reputation wouldn't increase much. It's very slow and has so many factors in play. 
    [*]Scouts are almost useless. The only good thing they can do is show you huge lists of potential wonderkids that will not become a star players in 9/10 cases. Sometimes you manage to dig a real gem there. Also, scouts' judgement of players ability and potential gives almost exactly the same reports when that grade is above 9.
    [*]Tactics. They are all over the place. AI doesn't need tactical familiarity to counter you yet if you try something new, you will be punished. Defensive tactics are terrible in this installment, leaking goals left and right with not much to offer in counter attacks. Yet AI perfectly parks the bus when it needs. Pre-made 4231 Gegenpress simply stomps the game.
    [*]Some matches are simply not meant to be won. Every now and then comes a match that simply isn't winnable, sometimes not even drawable. I've tried replaying those more than 20 times with many different tactics and results would be similar, despite my lower level sides managing to beat stronger opponents only months prior. 
    [*]Getting FM'd (losing or drawing last minute while dominating the whole game) occurs from time to time but unlike matches above, replaying them will have wildly different outcomes.
    [*]I don't care if real world statistic might back this feature up, but from FM19, present even today in FM21, every time without fail, on a day 2 days away from a matchday, at least one injury occurs. Micromanage every player's training, overload, rest, whatnot, every time, on a day 2 days away from a matchday, dreading message appears in the inbox informing you that at least one of your players (even U19 are included in this black magic) got injured and won't recover in time for said matchday. 
    [*]I dislike how player improvement works. Late bloomers basically don't exist. Jamie Vardy, van Dijk, Mahrez aren't possible as every player's ceiling is determined when they are created. And their development is over when they turn 24. Achievements do not lead to stat improvements which I think should be a feature. It's even realistic...  
[/list]
I've probably missed many other things but it's the gist of it.

The overwhelming positivity on the match engine surprises me as that has not been my experience at all. Sure the animations look a bit better and we see some dinks now but there are really disappointing things that happen on the defensive side of the game which lead me to believe that the ME has regressed.

Defenders are incapable of dealing with long balls WHEN AN OPPOSITION PLAYER IS NEAR THEM. They either miss the header, misjudge the flight of the ball and see it sail over their heads or just watch the forward control the ball and run past them for a 1v1 (deeper defensive line caused the last one to occur more). It happens far too often. 

Also, the way defenders attempt to deal with opposition players running directly at them with the ball is awful. More often than not they react appropriately when the opposition player is already past them (and by react appropriately i mean run fast to try to catch up with the player at which point they’ll bump into their heels because as far as I can see there still are no animations for physical battles between players). I thought defenders were going to be more aware of their surroundings this year but I am not seeing it. Sane gliding past the entire team and creating a 1v1 all by himself, regardless of where he received the ball and how many defenders are between him and the goal, happens far too often.

I know SI tried to buff the defensive side of the game because they knew it would be left behind due to the changes made to the attacking side but more work on that is still needed in my opinion.

The FM backheel where a player keeps the ball in play by backheeling it conveniently for an opposition player has been replaced by the FM bump the ball out of play this year. The FM backheel wasn’t even a problem in the last few versions of FM20 but the greatest FM ever has reintroduced it for reasons unknown. I have also seen a keeper save a shot from 6 yards when he was looking at the net instead of the ball so the ME doesn’t even factor the direction players are facing into the simulation.

I am not a fan of the new UI during a match. The players at the bottom of the screen in between highlights limit the amount of information displayed on the tablet if you dont minimise it so why was this not incorporated into the tablet? The dugout section has some useless information like the prompt to the change pen taker not disappearing after the pen is over or your assistant manager advising you to change from short to direct passing now being accompanied by a graphic of a pitch showing you all passes in the match which quickly turns into useless noise and does not disappear after a few seconds like in previous FM’s. The match stats on the left should be customizable like the match stats in the tablet section. The game doesn’t tell you who assisted a goal like before. Revisiting a game and viewing highlights or goals in the match, like a lot of other things, now takes more steps to do. Clicking individuals when attempting to give a team talk to a one or a few players pre ticks every player for some reason, which makes no sense. UI text scaling in the game doesn’t work properly so if you want to have as much info on the screen at one time as you did in FM20, you have to set the zoom so low that everything becomes much too small.

I listened to Miles when he said the gestures weren’t just the tone system in disguise. I’ve found them to be useful during player interactions but they add nothing more than what the tone system added to press conferences. Press conferences are still as useless as ever.

The game is a meh for me. There is a lot of football managing still there and I don’t have a reason to doubt that SI will update the game regularly and make it better as time goes on (especially ME) much like what happened to FM20 but as things stand currently I dont think the game/ME deserves the hype it is getting now.

At the time of this review, I've logged 254.5 hours of playtime. A large volume of that time has involved testing elements including the user interface and match engine, as opposed to playing the game normally. 

After purchasing every version of Football Manager, and its Championship Manager predecessor, FM 21 is the poorest iteration in the series. 

Somewhat controversially, the game is only a meagre update of FM 20 with some additional stats like xG sprinkled on top. While the game’s marketing materials suggest that the new innovations stretch to more complex interactions with the club’s board and squad, those are, at best, trivial and simply add more bloat to the standard user experience. 

With regards to the match engine, there have been the customary patches from the developer to correct a myriad of technical issues. All of which have been detrimental to the immersion of watching two teams play competitive football. However, this year’s offering stands out as recent patches to the game have caused further, more serious issues with the analysis of player performance. At present, there’s an issue where individual player ratings have been greatly reduced across the board. For experienced players of the series, it’s unusual to see players win end-of-season awards with average ratings between 7.1-7.25. 

Callum Wilson scored 35 goals in 35 games in my last season, an incredible haul, and barely scraped an average of 7.1. Full backs, wingers and central midfielders all suffer as the game doesn’t currently track key tackles, an important performance metric for players who aren’t scoring or creating. 

The animations reflected within the match engine have been increased in volume, but the player behaviour has become farcical. Defenders standing still when they can easily reach a ball first is a frequent occurrence and renders so much of the players tactical activity meaningless. The developer’s forum keeps a track of the list of issues which have been fixed and those that are still being worked upon. 

Another disappointing trend has been the number of clicks a user must make to access information which used to be easy to retrieve 5-6 years ago. The implementation of the ‘social’ tab where a large amount of the game’s news is hidden beneath has only grown in size with every new version. 

In the developer’s quest to be seen to bring innovation to the annual release, so much of that innovation is presented as affecting the most laborious aspects of the game. Press conferences. Player interactions. Board interactions. 

All of this leads to the user making more clicks in order to advance to the core managerial gameplay. Meanwhile, not enough innovation has been brought to the manner in which the match engine produces content. 

There’s also a disappointing lack of options for users to rearrange parts of the user interface to best suit their needs. The new match-day experience presents a vast amount of data through an extremely limited number of panels. Few of which are customisable. This creates a bottleneck of data visualisation which is so needless and easy to fix. 

This year, IGN came down hard of FIFA 21 for the Nintendo Switch for charging full price for what was essentially a threadbare update of FIFA 20 on that platform. Other review outlets did the same. Whilst there’s clearly been the challenge of developing during the pandemic, the game is a weak update of FM 20 with more than enough immersion-breaking bugs that the game simply cannot be recommended.

I don't want to give this game a negative review but I will until the following issues are fixed. Mainly because SI stated they were going to fix it but still have not, making the game incredibly difficult for me to play for extended periods. 

Some UI decisions have been questionable at best. They didn't even take into account those with poor vision or colourblindness, like myself. 

It's so hard for me to gauge my players fitness. They say "it was unrealistic to see a players fitness by a percentage". Well it's also unrealistic to know a players exact "reaction" after a shout. When I hear a manager shouting in real life on the side line - I don't see them take out a smiling emoji?!?!?! Nor do they smile, give a thumbs up or act delighted. 99% of footballers are so focused they totally ignore anything and the only reactions you do see are celebrations or anger fuelled by their adrenaline. So lets put this talk of "realism" on the back burner and put our eyesight and long term/extended play as a priority. If it aint broke, don't fix it.

Also regarding fitness etc. At least you hear managers say in real life "he's about 70% fit at the moment". Knowing a players "feelings" by body language is way more unrealistic - same as morale.

Some other UI decisions are weird - like the crooked "official team sheet" that represents data on an angle - totally triggering my OCD. Never present data on a weird angle - its ugly. 

Also when you do team talks - theres half the starting line up on the left and then the attackers along the top. Si stated and I quote "this is a bug we will be looking to fix for the full release". Still not fixed. Also highly triggers my OCD and it's just difficult to look at. This was perfectly fine on FM2020...just leave this stuff alone, seriously.

The match engine is a huge improvement but I still see a lot of "ping pong" rebounds and very odd decisions where players keep trying to all shoot into a wall of players. I almost felt compelled to make a video of it with pinball sounds as a joke. I also noticed that there is some match speed changes this year. Match speed at 50% feels like its in slow motion at times and 1 notch to the right seems too fast.

Match sounds (which have not been updated in over 15 years) have managed to regress again. It suddenly and abruptly cuts off during highlights - giving the game an unpolished feel. I know 99% of FM players play with the sound off but sound is a huge part of football - it's a huge part of the atmosphere. Covid has already taken this away from us in 2020, so please fix the sounds or work on a HUGE expansion to the sound in FM22!!! The only reason 99% of players play with the sound off is because its bad. They don't play with the sound off because they want to. If FM21 had similar sounds to say (FIFA or PES) they wouldn't play with the sounds off. This is the classic chicken or the egg question...you tell me this. How many people play FIFA or PES with the sound off. How many people play ANY game with the sound off?? That's right - not many - if any. Improve your sounds and you will see most people will play with the sound on. 

Selling players is incredibly difficult this year because they tried to add "covid" effects for realism. Look - either add Covid in FULLY into the game with empty stands, the actual virus and all of its effects in the game or leave this cruddy disease out of the game and allow us to forget about 2020 and enjoy a fantasy 2021. I think it should have been totally left out - with 0 effects from covid and allow us to enjoy the game normally, with normal finances and the ability to sell players at least for their value. It does make buying players easier, but then again - most clubs I have managed have a 0 budget to begin with...cause of covid! Thanks!! Can't even enjoy a fantasy.

Also match day camera angles. They now added a zoom to the TV view. This actually gives me a little bit of motion sickness and dizziness at times. I don't experience this with a real life game, but in a video game at 60fps it does make me feel a bit queasy. Please give us an option to turn this off or add more camera angles (like a manager first person view). This is the first FM where none of the camera angles are suitable for my enjoyment. Director Cam is actually fine, but I hate all the other weird and distant angles during corners and throw-ins. Again a director camera with a toggable "other views" would be good.

The other stuff is pretty good - its a big improvement compared to older FM's but some of these design and UI ideas and implementation doesn't take into account those with colourblindness and/or poor vision - causing eye strain during extended play.

As stated, the match engine has improved but its still a bit silly at times.

SI do the same thing year after year - they put in 110% effort and deliver a product to 90%. That extra 10% is always missing and eithe requires multiple patches until March to get things to maybe 95% or they let things slide for another year - then eventually letting things slide for over a decade (like sounds). They need a decent competitor to shoot a rocket up their butts to actually deliver 110% effort and a 110% product. For a full AAA price year after year - and one of the best sellers on STEAM - the old excuse of "we are just a small company" no longer suffices. This is a company that makes hundreds of millions of dollars and hiring some sound developers and giving the game a much larger improvement to atmosphere and graphics shouldn't be as slow as a progression as it has been. Ultimately this game still has graphics of a game from 2006 and sound from a game in the mid 90's. 

Again, this is a game that I love and pump a bunch of hours into - but at the same time - I expect more and I expect a polished product that takes into account people with vision issues, colourblindness, ocd and such.

I will update this to a positive review when they at least fix the UI as they promised. I won't hold my breath for the match sounds to be fixed but I hope that it will be a feature of FM22 "New and improved match day experience and atmosphere!".

My guess is that by FM2030, they still won't have updated sounds.

The match engine is an absolute beauty to watch, an amazing step up from 2020. I haven't screamed at the game for shot into the side netting for some time. The marking system overhaul is beautiful to see players intelligently cover space that others move from.  A lot of the goals are a lot more intelligently set up in the build up, it's very pleasing watching the football unfold.

One feature about the transfers- you can ask agents what would make their players available, and they'll tell you estimated salary and requests before you even make a deal with their team along with whether they'd want to join now or if they'd consider it after promotion. The scouting meetings actually feel like meetings and can help newer players recognize what they're lacking much easier, helping the game become more accessible.

The market has also been adjusted for covid, making players cheaper than ever and salaries affordable. I have only played until about February 2021 so far, but in a lower league save all these cheap deals, easy loans, and free agent players definitely allows you to get an easier step up.  According to SI this normalizes in a few years, so it'll be interesting to see how it unfolds.

My only complaint- some of the UI is some seriously clunky nonsense.  I'd rather have a more compact menu with coherent information rather than a flood of random tidbits taking up all of the space on the screen but I'm sure there will be mods to address this problem shortly after the game goes live.  Considering a number of areas of the game took considerable steps up along with some much needed QOL changes (auto ready unfit guys for u23 games? hells to the yes), I suppose not all the changes can be winners.

That being said, Having only started playing with FM19, this is the best looking and feeling iteration I've played. The whole match engine experience feels a lot more polished, and the games are more entertaining than ever to watch. If you've read this far, I'd like to say thank you for taking my review into consideration, and if you bought the game leave a comment and let me know how you're doing in your save. I'm curious to see others thoughts on the match engine as well.
